headline: Printmaking lets artists multiply their work—creating many originals from a single design
universal_truth: Reproduction changes access; what was rare for one becomes available to many
fun_facts: Before printmaking, every book had to be copied by hand—one at a time
Woodblock printing in China predates European printing by about 400 years
Andy Warhol's screen prints made 'multiple originals' a central artistic statement
discussion_questions: Is a print as 'original' as a painting?
How did the ability to reproduce images change culture?
What else in life becomes more valuable when shared?

hook.script: Before printing, every image had to be made one at a time—paintings were unique, books were hand-copied. Printmaking changed everything: create once, reproduce many. A single design could become hundreds of identical images.

cliff.script: Printing seems mechanical—press ink onto paper. But printmaking is a creative art form with its own techniques and aesthetics. What makes printmaking different from other visual arts?
cliff.prompt: What makes printmaking unique as an art form?

options.text: The artist creates in reverse—carving or drawing on a surface to make an image that transfers to paper as a mirror image
options.response: Yes. Printmakers think backwards—cutting away what stays white, inking what prints. This reversed thinking produces distinctive results.

options.text: Printmaking is faster than painting or drawing
options.response: Speed helps with reproduction, but the real distinction is the reversed creative process...

fact1.title: Thinking Backwards
fact1.script: Printmakers work in reverse. Letters must be carved backwards. What's cut away stays white; what remains takes ink. This mirror-image thinking is challenging but creates effects impossible in direct drawing.

fact2.title: Multiple Originals
fact2.script: Each print from a plate is an original—not a copy. Artists sign and number prints: 5/50 means the fifth print of fifty. Limited editions preserve value while allowing wider distribution. Originality multiplied.

fact3.title: Democratic Art
fact3.script: Prints democratized art. When paintings belonged only to the wealthy, prints brought images to ordinary people. Books, posters, newspapers—printmaking made visual culture accessible to everyone.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Reproduction changes access. Printmaking shows that what was rare for one becomes available to many. Sharing multiplies rather than divides. Some things gain value through wider distribution.

outro.script: That's Day 155. Tomorrow, we'll explore thinking with lines—drawing. Until then, consider what you create that could be shared with many.

growTrack.title: Shareable Creation - Multiply Your Impact
growTrack.learning_objective: Consider how to share your work more widely
growTrack.activity: What do you create that could be reproduced? Ideas, designs, systems, content? Like printmakers, consider how creating once and sharing many could multiply your impact. What could you 'print'?
